questions.questionText: A sells an article to B at a profit of 40%, and B sells it to C at a profit of 10%. If C pays Rs 924, what did A pay for it?

questions.questionText: A vendor buys 15 oranges for Rs 120 and sells 12 oranges for Rs 120. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.explanation: CP per orange = 120/15 = 8. SP per orange = 120/12 = 10. Change = (10 - 8)/8 x 100 = 25%, a 25% profit.

questions.questionText: If the cost price of 12 articles is equal to the selling price of 8 articles, what is the profit or loss percent?

questions.shortcut: Profit % = (m - n)/n x 100 when m > n; loss % = (n - m)/n x 100 when m < n.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper wants to earn a profit of 35% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price. By what percent must he mark up the cost price?

questions.questionText: A trader buys goods worth Rs 22000. He sells two-fifths of them at a profit of 20% and the remaining at a loss of 20%. What is his net profit or loss in rupees?
questions.explanation: Profit on the first part = 8800 x 20% = 1760. Loss on the rest = 13200 x 20% = 2640. Net = Rs 880 loss.
questions.shortcut: Split the total cost into the two parts first, then compute each part's gain or loss separately.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper buys a table for Rs 1950 and sells it for Rs 2535. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.shortcut: Profit or loss percent is always calculated on the COST price, not the selling price.

questions.questionText: A jacket is marked at Rs 2400. A discount of 15% is offered. What is the selling price?
questions.shortcut: SP = 85% of marked price = 2400 x 85/100.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper wants to earn a profit of 30% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price. By what percent must he mark up the cost price?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100. Needed SP = 130. Marked price M satisfies 80% of M = 130, so M = 130 x 100/80 = 162.5. Mark-up = 62.5%.
questions.shortcut: Marked price = desired SP / (1 - discount). Do not just add the two percentages.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper marks an article at Rs 4300 and allows successive discounts of 15% and 25%. If the cost price of the article is Rs 1500, what is his profit or loss percent?
questions.shortcut: Apply the two discounts one after the other (multiply the factors), then compare SP with CP.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells wheat at cost price but his false weight makes him gain 25%. How many grams does his '1 kg' weight actually weigh?
questions.explanation: Let the weight be w g. (1000 - w)/w x 100 = 25, so 1000/w = 1.25 and w = 800 g.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above cost. What rate of discount must he allow to earn a profit of 19%?
questions.explanation: Let CP = 100, marked = 140. SP needed = 119. Discount = (140 - 119)/140 x 100 = 15%.
questions.shortcut: SP/Marked = 119/140; discount = 1 minus that ratio.

questions.questionText: A man buys a school bag for Rs 27000, spends Rs 1300 on repairs and then sells it for Rs 33960. What is his profit or loss percent?
questions.shortcut: Add overheads (repairs, transport) to the cost price before finding the percentage.
